claims.claim: **Intranasal fentanyl is a safe, non-invasive, effective analgesic for moderate to severe pain**, used alongside non-drug and other drug pain management.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Onset within 5 minutes; lasts about 30–60 minutes.** Prescribe in consultation with a senior clinician.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use it as first analgesia when a child of 12 months or older has moderate to severe pain and no IV access** — for burns, fractures, dislocations, amputations, significant lacerations, sickle cell crisis, surgical pain, and painful procedures under nitrous oxide.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Contraindications:** altered conscious state · known hypersensitivity to fentanyl · younger than 12 months · active epistaxis · both nasal passages occluded.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **With nitrous oxide:** give fentanyl **5 minutes before** starting nitrous oxide sedation; the combination **increases the risk of vomiting**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Document a baseline pain score, sedation score and set of observations** before giving it.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **UMSS:** 0 = awake, alert · 1 = minimal sedation · 2 = moderate sedation, easily roused by light touch or simple command · 3 = deep sedation, rousable only by significant physical stimulation · 4 = unrousable.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **The child must be awake or easily roused to voice (UMSS 0–1) before each dose.** Monitor heart rate, respiratory rate, oxygen saturation, pain and sedation scores.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If sedated or vital signs are abnormal**, tell the treating clinician and continue observations until back to baseline. **After the last dose, do two further sets of observations 5 minutes apart.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **First dose: 1.5 microg/kg, max 100 microg**, using the 300 microg/mL nasal solution. **Use ideal body weight for overweight children.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **The usual maximum is 75 micrograms** with the 100 microg/2 mL concentration (volume limits); **100 micrograms** only with the hospital-only 300 microg/mL solution.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Second dose (optional), 5–10 minutes after the first: 0.75–1.5 microg/kg, to a max of 75–100 microg.** Then review and consider IV access for further analgesia.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Draw up the dose plus 0.1 mL for the first dose** to prime the atomiser dead space; **not for the second dose** when re-using the device.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Sit the child at about 45 degrees** (or head to one side), **press the plunger quickly** so it atomises rather than drips, ask for only a gentle sniff, and **divide the dose between nostrils**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Side effects are uncommon:** sedation, respiratory depression, hypotension, nausea and vomiting (more with nitrous oxide), pruritus. Chest wall rigidity is reported only with large IV doses.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Opioid toxicity:** immediate senior review and move to resuscitation · stop further opioid · support airway and oxygenate · assist ventilation as required · give naloxone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Naloxone:** **excessive sedation (UMSS 3): 1–5 microg/kg IM or IV (max 100 microg)**, repeated every 2–3 minutes if needed · **acute overdose (UMSS 4): 10 microg/kg, max 400 microg** · **no response to 10 microg/kg: 100 microg/kg, max 2 mg**.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Consider discharge when sedation score and observations are back to baseline** and the pain score is minimal and manageable with simple analgesics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, Clinical Practice Guidelines: 'Intranasal fentanyl' (Last updated October 2025), at https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Intranasal_fentanyl/, retrieved 2026-09-23
